content.text: {"quote_faithful": "yes", "verdict": "confirmed", "evidence_kind": "invalid_inference", "fatal": "no", "explanation": "The quote is verbatim and does mean what the objector says: v(B) was defined (Section 4) as the nested difference taken in the *decreasing* order b_1\u2265\u2026\u2265b_r, and the strategy then processes b_2,\u2026,b_r 'in turn', i.e. in that order. But the proof of Theorem 4.2 only produces, via Lemma 4.1, *some* ordering of P\u222aN whose nested difference equals g; it never shows the decreasing order attains it. Decreasing order is not optimal in general: for {8,7,6,5,4} the decreasing nested value is ||||8-7|-6|-5|-4| = 4, while the ordering 8,4,6,7,5 gives 0. So the inference 'Theorem 4.2 \u21d2 v(B) (decreasing) \u2264 T_n' does not follow. Not fatal: the running-value procedure, cut count, distinctness and parity cancellation are all order-agnostic, so processing B in the ordering Lemma 4.1 already constructs repairs the step verbatim."}
